mapAttribution: Schematic kingdom/empire extents for Europa Strata — not cadastral or modern state borders. Rings approximate political control at tick years (Euratlas/Shepherd-informed; coast templates from Natural Earth-style Europe polygons).
narrative: From the Dutch Revolt’s consolidation and the Thirty Years’ War through Westphalia, Bourbon–Habsburg rivalry, Sweden’s Baltic rise and fall, Russia’s empire, Ottoman retreat from Hungary, Prussian ascent, and the First Partition of Poland—Europe’s map on the eve of the French Revolution is a system of composite monarchies and commercial republics, not nation-states.

polities.name: Kingdom of France
polities.description: Bourbon France consolidates after Nantes, then builds a fiscal-military absolutist state under Louis XIII/XIV. Frontiers push east and south through Westphalia, the Pyrenees, and Nijmegen; Lorraine and Corsica close the pre-revolutionary outline. By 1789 the Old Regime still rules a nearly modern hexagonal kingdom on the eve of revolution.
polities.conflicts: Thirty Years’ War interventions; Franco-Spanish War; Dutch War; Nine Years’ War; War of the Spanish Succession; War of the Austrian Succession; Seven Years’ War; American Revolutionary War alliance.
polities.leaders: Henry IV; Louis XIII; Cardinal Richelieu; Louis XIV; Louis XV; Louis XVI; ministers Colbert, Fleury, Choiseul.
polities.religion: Catholic monarchy; Edict of Nantes (1598) then Revocation (1685); Gallican church under royal control; Huguenot diaspora after 1685.
polities.culture: Classical French court culture (Versailles), academies, Cartesian and Enlightenment letters, and a Paris-centered language of state.

polities.name: Kingdom of England
polities.description: Stuart England enters personal union with Scotland (1603) while remaining a separate kingdom. Civil wars, Commonwealth, and Restoration remake the constitution; the 1688–89 settlement limits the crown. Mapped separately until the 1707 union creates Great Britain.
polities.conflicts: Eighty Years’ War aid; Civil Wars (1642–51); Anglo-Dutch Wars; Nine Years’ War; War of the Spanish Succession opening.
polities.leaders: Elizabeth I (edge); James I; Charles I; Cromwell; Charles II; James II; William III & Mary II; Anne.
polities.religion: Established Church of England; Puritan and Catholic conflicts; Toleration Act (1689) for Trinitarian Protestants.
polities.culture: Shakespearean afterglow into Jacobean/Caroline letters, scientific revolution (Royal Society), and commercial-maritime expansion.

polities.name: Kingdom of Scotland
polities.description: Independent kingdom in personal union with England from 1603. Presbyterian settlement and Covenanting politics define the century; parliamentary union with England in 1707 ends separate statehood on the map.
polities.conflicts: Bishops’ Wars; Wars of the Three Kingdoms; Jacobite risings after union (post-map as Scotland).
polities.leaders: James VI/I; Charles I; Covenanter regimes; Charles II; William II (III of England); Anne.
polities.religion: Presbyterian Kirk dominant after Reformation; episcopal experiments under Stuarts provoke revolt.
polities.culture: Gaelic Highlands and Scots Lowlands; universities and early Enlightenment precursors in Edinburgh/Glasgow.

polities.name: Kingdom of Great Britain
polities.description: England and Scotland united by the 1707 Act of Union. Hanoverian Britain becomes Europe’s leading naval-commercial power, fighting France in successive coalition wars while building a parliamentary fiscal state.
polities.conflicts: War of the Spanish Succession (closing); Austrian Succession; Seven Years’ War; American Revolutionary War; opening French Revolutionary Wars (from 1792).
polities.leaders: Anne; Georges I–III; ministers Walpole, Pitt the Elder, North, Pitt the Younger.
polities.religion: Anglican establishment in England; Presbyterian Scotland; Catholic disabilities; Methodist revival.
polities.culture: Augustan and Enlightenment Britain—coffee-house politics, political economy, and global trading companies.

polities.name: Kingdom of Ireland
polities.description: Separate kingdom in personal union with England/Britain. Tudor/Stuart conquest, plantations, Confederate and Williamite wars, and Penal Laws structure a Protestant Ascendancy over a Catholic majority.
polities.conflicts: Nine Years’ War (Tyrone); 1641 rising & Cromwellian conquest; Williamite War (1689–91); 1798 Rebellion (just after 1789 tick).
polities.leaders: Lord Deputies/Lieutenants; James II in exile campaign; Grattan-era Patriot politics in the Dublin Parliament.
polities.religion: Official Protestant (Church of Ireland); Catholic majority under Penal restrictions; Presbyterian Ulster.
polities.culture: Gaelic and Anglo-Irish literatures; colonial estate society; Dublin as second city of the early British world.

polities.name: Spanish Monarchy
polities.yearsActive: Habsburg composite to 1700; Bourbon Spain thereafter
polities.description: Philip III–IV still rule a European composite (Iberia, Italy, Franche-Comté, Spanish Netherlands) alongside a vast empire. The War of the Spanish Succession breaks the Habsburg bloc; Bourbon Spain can keep the peninsula and colonies but loses the European outer rings at Utrecht (1713–14).
polities.conflicts: Eighty Years’ War; Thirty Years’ War; Franco-Spanish War; War of the Spanish Succession; later Italian and colonial wars.
polities.leaders: Philip III; Philip IV; Charles II; Philip V; Ferdinand VI; Charles III; Charles IV.
polities.religion: Catholic monarchy; Inquisition; Jesuits expelled under Charles III reform era.
polities.culture: Late Siglo de Oro into Bourbon ilustración; Madrid court and American silver fiscal dependence.

polities.name: Kingdom of Portugal
polities.description: Mapped as Portugal throughout. Dynastic union with Spain (1580–1640) ends in the Restoration War; independent Braganza Portugal rebuilds Atlantic empire while remaining a European secondary power allied increasingly with Britain.
polities.conflicts: Dutch-Portuguese colonial wars; Restoration War vs Spain; Seven Years’ War Iberian campaign; French Revolutionary/Napoleonic crisis ahead.
polities.leaders: Philip II–III of Spain (union); John IV of Braganza; John V; Joseph I; Pombal; Maria I.
polities.religion: Catholic; Inquisition; Pombaline reform of church property.
polities.culture: Lisbon commercial culture; Brazilian gold boom; Pombaline neoclassical rebuilding after 1755 earthquake.

polities.name: Lower Navarre
polities.yearsActive: French Navarre rump to early Bourbon absorption
polities.description: Tiny trans-Pyrenean rump of Navarre held with the French crown (Henry IV’s patrimony). Shown at 1600 only as the last distinct Navarrese outline before full administrative merger into France.
polities.conflicts: Absorbed into French provincial structure rather than field warfare in this era.
polities.leaders: Henry IV; Louis XIII.
polities.religion: Catholic after Wars of Religion settlement; earlier Calvinist court under Jeanne d’Albret.
polities.culture: Basque-Romance border society under French sovereignty.

polities.name: Dutch Republic (United Provinces)
polities.description: Federal Calvinist commercial republic. Independence recognized at Westphalia (1648). Golden Age naval and financial power peaks mid-century, then faces Anglo-French pressure; still independent at 1789 before the Batavian Revolution (1795).
polities.conflicts: Eighty Years’ War; Anglo-Dutch Wars; Franco-Dutch War; War of the Spanish Succession; Fourth Anglo-Dutch War.
polities.leaders: Maurice & Frederick Henry of Nassau; Johan de Witt; William III; later stadtholders of Orange.
polities.religion: Public Reformed church; notable confessional pluralism in cities.
polities.culture: Dutch Golden Age art, cartography, stock exchange, and global VOC/WIC companies.

polities.name: Spanish Netherlands
polities.description: Catholic southern Low Countries retained by Spain after the Dutch Revolt. A fortified buffer repeatedly fought over by France and the Dutch; transferred to the Austrian Habsburgs at Utrecht/Rastatt.
polities.conflicts: Eighty Years’ War; Franco-Dutch War; Nine Years’ War; War of the Spanish Succession.
polities.leaders: Spanish governors-general (e.g. Isabella & Albert; later viceroys under Philip IV/Charles II).
polities.religion: Tridentine Catholicism; Counter-Reformation stronghold.
polities.culture: Flemish Baroque (Rubens) under Habsburg court patronage at Brussels.

polities.name: Austrian Netherlands
polities.description: Former Spanish Netherlands awarded to Austria after the War of the Spanish Succession. Governed as a Habsburg possession with local estates; restive under Joseph II’s reforms by the late 1780s.
polities.conflicts: War of the Austrian Succession (French occupation episodes); Brabant Revolution (1789–90).
polities.leaders: Charles VI; Maria Theresa; Joseph II; local governors in Brussels.
polities.religion: Catholic; Josephist church reforms provoke resistance.
polities.culture: Late Baroque/Rococo Brussels and Antwerp under Austrian administration.

polities.name: Holy Roman Empire
polities.description: Decentralized empire of German, Bohemian, and Alpine estates. Westphalia (1648) confirms territorial sovereignty of princes and recognizes Dutch and Swiss exits. Still the constitutional frame of Central Europe in 1789, though great-power politics is driven by Austria and Prussia.
polities.conflicts: Thirty Years’ War; later Franco-imperial wars; Austrian Succession; Seven Years’ War as imperial civil/great-power war.
polities.leaders: Emperors Rudolf II; Ferdinand II/III; Leopold I; Charles VI; Francis I; Joseph II; Leopold II (from 1790).
polities.religion: Cuius regio after Augsburg/Westphalia; Catholic, Lutheran, and Reformed estates.
polities.culture: Imperial free cities, princely courts, and Baroque church culture across a mosaic of sovereignties.

polities.name: Habsburg Monarchy (Austria)
polities.description: Danubian Habsburg composite: Alpine hereditary lands, then Bohemian crown, reconquered Hungary after 1683–99, and after Utrecht the Austrian Netherlands and Milan. First Partition adds Galicia (1772). The great rival of Ottoman and later Prussian power.
polities.conflicts: Long Turkish War aftermath; Great Turkish War; War of the Spanish Succession; Austrian Succession; Seven Years’ War; War of the Bavarian Succession.
polities.leaders: Ferdinand II/III; Leopold I; Charles VI; Maria Theresa; Joseph II; Kaunitz.
polities.religion: Catholic dynasty; Contre-Reformation in Bohemia/Hungary; Josephist toleration patents late century.
polities.culture: Vienna as imperial-musical capital; multiethnic estate monarchy spanning German, Czech, Magyar, Italian, and Netherlandish lands.

polities.name: Brandenburg–Prussia / Kingdom of Prussia
polities.description: Hohenzollern Brandenburg united with Ducal Prussia, gains at Westphalia, then royal title (1701). Frederick II seizes Silesia (1740s); First Partition adds West Prussia (1772), linking the kingdom’s cores. Militarized bureaucratic state and great power by 1789.
polities.conflicts: Thirty Years’ War; Swedish-Brandenburg wars; Silesian Wars / Austrian Succession; Seven Years’ War; War of the Bavarian Succession.
polities.leaders: Elector Frederick William (Great Elector); Frederick I; Frederick William I; Frederick II (the Great).
polities.religion: Calvinist dynasty over Lutheran majority; later limited toleration.
polities.culture: Potsdam/Berlin military-administrative culture; early German Enlightenment under Frederick II.

polities.name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
polities.description: Elective noble republic at vast eastern extent c. 1600–1648. Mid-century wars (Sweden, Muscovy, Cossack/Ukrainian) and the early-eighteenth crisis weaken it; First Partition (1772) truncates the map by 1789, with further partitions ahead (1793–95).
polities.conflicts: Polish–Swedish wars; Khmelnytsky Uprising; Russo-Polish wars; Great Northern War; War of the Polish Succession; Bar Confederation.
polities.leaders: Sigismund III; Władysław IV; John II Casimir; John III Sobieski; Saxon kings Augustus II/III; Stanisław August Poniatowski.
polities.religion: Catholic political nation; large Orthodox, Uniate, Protestant, and Jewish populations; Warsaw Confederation tradition of confessional coexistence under strain.
polities.culture: Sarmatian noble culture, Latin/Polish letters, and a uniquely elective, liberum-veto parliamentary system.

polities.name: Swedish Empire / Kingdom of Sweden
polities.yearsActive: Baltic great-power age c. 1611–1721; kingdom continues
polities.description: Vasa/Palatinate Sweden builds a Baltic empire—Finland, Estonia/Livonia, Ingria, and German bridgeheads after Westphalia. Collapse after the Great Northern War (Nystad 1721) returns Sweden to a Sweden–Finland kingdom with only minor Pomeranian remnants.
polities.conflicts: Ingrian/Polish wars; Thirty Years’ War; Northern Wars; Scanian War; Great Northern War; later Russo-Swedish wars.
polities.leaders: Charles IX; Gustavus Adolphus; Christina; Charles X Gustav; Charles XI; Charles XII; Gustavian kings.
polities.religion: Lutheran state church.
polities.culture: Military allotment state, Baltic administrative culture, and later Gustavian neoclassicism.

polities.name: Denmark–Norway
polities.description: Oldenburg dual monarchy. Holds Scania until Roskilde (1658); thereafter Denmark–Norway proper plus Schleswig-Holstein dynastic ties. Secondary Baltic power after Swedish ascendancy.
polities.conflicts: Kalmar War; Torstenson War; Scanian War; Great Northern War; later Napoleonic crisis ahead.
polities.leaders: Christian IV; Frederick III (absolutism 1660); later Oldenburg kings.
polities.religion: Lutheran state churches.
polities.culture: Copenhagen absolutist court; Norwegian resource periphery; Sound Toll revenues.

polities.name: Tsardom / Russian Empire
polities.description: Muscovite recovery after the Time of Troubles, then westward and southward expansion: left-bank Ukraine, Baltic provinces after Nystad, partitions of Poland, and Crimea (1783). By 1789 a Eurasian empire anchoring eastern Europe.
polities.conflicts: Polish–Muscovite wars; Russo-Swedish wars; Great Northern War; Russo-Turkish wars; participation in Polish partitions.
polities.leaders: Boris Godunov; early Romanovs; Alexis; Peter I; Elizabeth; Catherine II.
polities.religion: Russian Orthodox state church; Nikonian schism; later limited multi-confessional imperial practice.
polities.culture: From Muscovite court ritual to Petrine/Catherinian Europeanizing empire—St Petersburg as new capital (1703).

polities.name: Ottoman Empire (European lands)
polities.description: Still holds the Balkans and central Hungarian corridor c. 1600–1648. Great Turkish War and Karlowitz (1699) surrender most of Hungary/Transylvania to the Habsburgs; eighteenth-century wars trim further edges while Rumelia and Greece remain Ottoman into 1789.
polities.conflicts: Long Turkish War aftermath; Cretan War; Great Turkish War; wars with Venice/Habsburgs/Russia; later Russo-Turkish wars.
polities.leaders: Mehmed III; Ahmed I; Murad IV; Mehmed IV; later 18th-c. sultans; Köprülü viziers.
polities.religion: Sunni Islamic empire; millet system for Orthodox, Armenian, Jewish communities; Muslim elites in Balkans.
polities.culture: Classical Ottoman court culture at Istanbul; provincial ayans rising in the eighteenth century.

polities.name: Royal Hungary
polities.description: Habsburg-controlled western/northern remnant of the medieval Hungarian crown, pressed between Ottoman Hungary and Transylvania. After Karlowitz the reconquered lands are shown within the Habsburg Monarchy layer.
polities.conflicts: Ottoman frontier wars; Fifteen Years’ War echoes; Rákóczi period ahead after 1700.
polities.leaders: Habsburg kings Ferdinand II/III; Hungarian estates and palatines.
polities.religion: Catholic Habsburg restoration vs Protestant nobles; Orthodox minorities in south.
polities.culture: Magyar noble estate politics under Habsburg kingship; fortress frontier society.

polities.name: Principality of Transylvania
polities.description: Semi-independent principality under Ottoman suzerainty, a Protestant power-broker in the Thirty Years’ War era. Habsburg incorporation follows the Great Turkish War; not mapped separately after 1648 in this pack.
polities.conflicts: Anti-Habsburg campaigns (Bethlen, György Rákóczi I); Ottoman–Habsburg wars.
polities.leaders: Stephen Bocskai; Gábor Bethlen; György Rákóczi I/II; Mihály Apafi.
polities.religion: Recognized Catholic, Reformed, Lutheran, Unitarian estates; Orthodox Romanians numerous.
polities.culture: Multiethnic Carpathian principality with strong Magyar Reformed elite culture.

polities.name: Lands of the Bohemian Crown
polities.description: Bohemia, Moravia, and Silesia under Habsburg kings. The 1618 Defenestration ignites the Thirty Years’ War; White Mountain (1620) breaks the revolt. Silesia is later seized by Prussia (1740s)—hence Bohemia layer stops at 1700 while Austria/Prussia carry later change.
polities.conflicts: Bohemian Revolt; Thirty Years’ War; later Silesian loss under Maria Theresa.
polities.leaders: Frederick V (Winter King); Ferdinand II; later Habsburg sovereigns.
polities.religion: Forced re-Catholicization after 1620; Protestant exile.
polities.culture: Czech lands under Baroque re-Catholicization; Germanization of elites.

polities.name: Swiss Confederation
polities.yearsActive: De facto independence long before; recognized 1648
polities.description: Loose confederation of cantons. Westphalia recognizes independence from the Empire. Remains outside great-power partitions, supplying mercenaries and guarding armed neutrality.
polities.conflicts: Internal confessional tensions (e.g. Villmergen wars); generally avoids great-power wars.
polities.leaders: Cantonal councils; Tagsatzung diet.
polities.religion: Catholic and Reformed cantons in armed coexistence.
polities.culture: Alpine republican particularism; mercenary export; early modern print and scientific culture in cities like Basel/Geneva.

polities.name: Republic of Venice
polities.description: Maritime republic with terraferma, Dalmatian coasts, and (until mid/late 17th c.) Crete. Slowly loses eastern empire to the Ottomans while remaining a distinct Italian power until Napoleonic extinction (1797).
polities.conflicts: Cretan War (1645–69); Morean War; later Ottoman wars; French Revolutionary invasion ahead.
polities.leaders: Doges and patrician councils (Great Council, Senate).
polities.religion: Catholic; distinctive Venetian church privileges.
polities.culture: Late Renaissance into Baroque/Rococo Venice—opera, painting, and Adriatic commerce in relative decline.

polities.name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
polities.description: Medici grand duchy centered on Florence, later passing to Francis of Lorraine (1737) and Habsburg-Lorraine secondary rule. A stable mid-sized Italian state through 1789.
polities.conflicts: War of the Spanish Succession orbit; generally secondary Italian diplomacy.
polities.leaders: Cosimo II; Ferdinando II; Cosimo III; Gian Gastone; Francis Stephen; Peter Leopold (reformer).
polities.religion: Catholic; Leopoldine reform of church institutions.
polities.culture: Florentine academies, science (Galileo patronage earlier), and Enlightenment reform under Peter Leopold.

polities.name: Duchy of Milan
polities.yearsActive: Spanish then Austrian Habsburg possession in this era
polities.description: Wealthy Lombard duchy under Spanish Habsburgs through the seventeenth century, then Austrian after Utrecht. Remains a key Habsburg Italian possession in 1750–1789.
polities.conflicts: Franco-Spanish Italian wars echoes; War of the Spanish Succession; War of the Austrian Succession.
polities.leaders: Spanish governors; Austrian Habsburg administration under Charles VI/Maria Theresa/Joseph II.
polities.religion: Catholic; Borromean Counter-Reformation legacy.
polities.culture: Lombard urban wealth; later Austrian-enlightened administration in Milan.

polities.name: Papal States
polities.description: Temporal territories of the pope across Lazio, Umbria, Marche, and Romagna. Survive as a distinct sovereignty through early modern Italian wars into 1789.
polities.conflicts: Castro wars earlier; War of the Spanish Succession alignments; later French Revolutionary pressure.
polities.leaders: Popes from Clement VIII through Pius VI in this span.
polities.religion: Catholic theocracy; Tridentine reform center.
polities.culture: Baroque Rome as artistic capital of Catholic Europe.

polities.name: Kingdom of Naples
polities.description: Southern Italian kingdom under Spanish Habsburg viceroys (with Sicily often linked). After the Succession War it passes briefly to Austria, then to Bourbon rulers who reunite Naples and Sicily—shown as Two Sicilies from 1750.
polities.conflicts: Masaniello revolt (1647); Succession War; later Bourbon consolidation.
polities.leaders: Spanish viceroys under Philip III/IV/Charles II.
polities.religion: Catholic; strong baronial and clerical society.
polities.culture: Naples as a major European city—music, law, and southern Baroque.

polities.name: Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
polities.description: Bourbon Charles (later Charles III of Spain) takes Naples and Sicily in the 1730s. Mapped 1750–1789 as the united southern Italian Bourbon kingdom (formal ‘Two Sicilies’ name consolidates later).
polities.conflicts: War of the Polish Succession Italian theatre; later French Revolutionary wars.
polities.leaders: Charles of Bourbon; Ferdinand IV/III.
polities.religion: Catholic monarchy.
polities.culture: Naples Enlightenment (Genovesi) and Bourbon court absolutism; Palermo as Sicilian capital.

polities.name: Republic of Genoa
polities.description: Ligurian maritime republic; holds Corsica until sale to France (1768). Banking and Mediterranean trade sustain a shrinking political footprint.
polities.conflicts: Corsican revolts (Paoli); French pressure; later Napoleonic end.
polities.leaders: Doges of the oligarchic republic.
polities.religion: Catholic.
polities.culture: Genoese mercantile aristocracy; Corsican resistance culture under Paoli.

polities.name: Savoy / Kingdom of Sardinia
polities.yearsActive: Duchy of Savoy; Kingdom of Sardinia from 1720
polities.description: Alpine Savoy-Piedmont rises through clever diplomacy in the Succession wars; gains Sardinia and royal title (1720). By 1750–1789 the Savoyard state is a compact Italian kingdom spanning Piedmont, Savoy, Nice, and Sardinia.
polities.conflicts: Thirty Years’ War orbit; War of the Spanish Succession; War of the Austrian Succession; later Revolutionary wars.
polities.leaders: Charles Emmanuel I; Victor Amadeus II; Charles Emmanuel III; Victor Amadeus III.
polities.religion: Catholic; Waldensian minority under pressure.
polities.culture: Turin military-absolutist court; Alpine-Italian administrative state.

polities.name: Crimean Khanate
polities.description: Giray khanate on the Crimean steppe under Ottoman suzerainty; slave-raiding and cavalry power on Russia’s southern frontier. Annexed by Catherine II in 1783—absent at the 1789 tick.
polities.conflicts: Russo-Crimean wars; Ottoman–Russian wars as vassal.
polities.leaders: Giray khans under Ottoman oversight.
polities.religion: Sunni Islam.
polities.culture: Tatar steppe khanate culture linking Black Sea and Ottoman worlds.

polities.name: Principality of Wallachia
polities.description: Danubian principality under Ottoman suzerainty, ruled by native and later Phanariot princes. Remains a distinct vassal polity on the map through 1789.
polities.conflicts: Ottoman–Habsburg wars on its borders; anti-Ottoman risings episodic.
polities.leaders: Native dynasts then Phanariot hospodars from the early eighteenth century.
polities.religion: Eastern Orthodox.
polities.culture: Romanian Orthodox princely culture between Ottoman, Habsburg, and Russian pressures.

polities.name: Principality of Moldavia
polities.description: Eastern Carpathian principality under Ottoman suzerainty. Bukovina is ceded to Austria in 1775; the core remains an Ottoman vassal at 1789.
polities.conflicts: Polish, Ottoman, and Russian wars across Moldavian land; Habsburg annexation of Bukovina.
polities.leaders: Native princes; Phanariot hospodars in the eighteenth century.
polities.religion: Eastern Orthodox.
polities.culture: Romanian Orthodox culture with strong Polish and Ottoman diplomatic entanglement.
